connect.pos: Noun (the place) + action verb, ます form

examples.ja: [学校|がっこう]{で}[日本語|にほんご]をべんきょうします。
[駅|えき]の[前|まえ]の[店|みせ]{で}パンを[買|か]います。
examples.en: I buy bread at the shop in front of the station.

watch.note: で is for the place where you do something. あります and います only say where a thing or a person is, so that place takes に: 学校に としょかんが あります.
watch.bad: 学校でとしょかんがあります。
watch.good: 学校にとしょかんがあります。

examples.ja: はし{で}[魚|さかな]を[食|た]べます。
[毎日|まいにち][電車|でんしゃ]{で}[会社|かいしゃ]へ[行|い]きます。
examples.en: I go to work by train every day.

watch.note: With 行きます, the bus is how you go, so it takes で. バスに goes with a different verb: バスに のります (get on the bus).
watch.bad: バスに学校へ行きます。
watch.good: バスで学校へ行きます。

compare.intro: All three come right after a noun. で says where you do something or what you use; に with あります says where a thing is.

forms.tag: するところ · where you do it
forms.ja: [学校|がっこう]{で}[本|ほん]を[読|よ]みます。

forms.tag: あるところ · where it is
forms.ja: [学校|がっこう]{に}[本|ほん]がたくさんあります。
forms.en: There are a lot of books at school.

forms.tag: つかうもの · what you use
forms.ja: ペン{で}[名前|なまえ]を[書|か]きます。
forms.en: I write my name with a pen.

check.label: 学校の店
check.q: [学校|がっこう]の[中|なか]に[店|みせ]があります。その[店|みせ]（　　）^パンを[買|か]います^。
why: に says where a thing is, with あります. Here you do something there: 買います.
パンを already has を. その店を パンを has two を and makes no sense.
Buying is an action, so the shop where you buy takes で.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: わたしは[毎日|まいにち]うち（　　）^テレビを[見|み]ます^。
why: 見ます is an action, so the place where you watch takes で: at home.
に would say where something is. Watching TV is an action, so に does not fit.
テレビを already has を. うちを テレビを has two を.
うちが would make the house the one watching TV.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: きょうしつ（　　）^つくえやいすがあります^。
why: あります here says where desks and chairs are. That is not an action, so で does not fit.
Where things are takes に before あります: in the classroom.
あります does not take を.
へ shows a direction you go to. あります is not going anywhere.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: はし（　　）^ごはんを[食|た]べます^。
why: ごはんを already has を. はしを ごはんを has two を.
はしに does not say what you eat with.
Chopsticks are what you use to eat, so they take で.
はしと ごはんを would mean you eat the chopsticks and the rice.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: わたしは[毎日|まいにち][電車|でんしゃ]（　　）^[会社|かいしゃ]へ[行|い]きます^。
why: 行きます does not take を for the train here.
電車と would mean you go together with the train, like with a friend.
電車に goes with のります (get on). With 行きます it does not fit.
The train is how you go, so it takes で: by train.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: [山川|やまかわ]さんは[毎日|まいにち]バス
drill.hint: First say how Ms. Yamakawa comes, then where she comes to, then the verb.
drill.full: [山川|やまかわ]さんは[毎日|まいにち]バス{で}[学校|がっこう]へ[来|き]ますよ。
drill.explain: バスで is how she comes. 学校へ is where she comes to, and 来ます goes last, right before よ.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: [中山|なかやま]さんはいつも[駅|えき]の[前|まえ]の[店|みせ]
drill.hint: The shop is where the action happens. Then what is bought, then the verb.
drill.full: [中山|なかやま]さんはいつも[駅|えき]の[前|まえ]の[店|みせ]{で}パンを[買|か]います。
drill.explain: 店で is where Mr. Nakayama buys. パンを is what he buys, and 買います comes last.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: きのう　デパート（　　）　くつを　買いました。
exam.explain: Buying is an action, so the place where you buy takes で: デパートで 買いました. に would say where something is, くつを already has を, and へ shows the direction you go to, which needs a verb like 行きました.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: この　かみには　えんぴつ（　　）　名前を　書きます。
exam.explain: The pencil is what you write with, so it takes で. 名前を already has を, えんぴつが would make the pencil the writer, and へ shows a direction.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.full: A「きのう　学校{で}　何を　食べましたか。」　B「カレーです。」
exam.explain: で, 何, を, 食べました: what did you eat at school yesterday? 学校で is where the eating happened, 何を asks what was eaten, and B answers カレーです.

scene.en: A notice at a community centre
scene.intro: Tap each word on the notice about this week's Japanese classes.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: 土よう日の　_午後_は　日本語の　クラスが　あります。
check.explain: 午後 is ごご, afternoon. ごぜん is 午前 (morning). こご and ごこう are not words; both kanji here are read ご.

skill.ask: Where does Lin eat lunch on Fridays?
skill.passage: リンさんは　わたしの　クラスの　友だちです。毎日　電車で　学校へ　来ます。ひるごはんは　いつも　学校の　しょくどうで　食べますが、^金よう日は　学校の　前の　こうえんで^　食べます。よるは　うちで　日本語の　本を　読みます。
skill.strategy: Find ひるごはん, then read past が to see where Lin eats on 金よう日.

item.q: リンさんは　金よう日に　どこで　ひるごはんを　食べますか。
options: 学校の　しょくどう
学校の　前の　こうえん
えきの　前の　店
item.explain: Lin usually eats lunch in the school cafeteria, but the sentence after が says 金よう日は 学校の 前の こうえんで 食べます: on Fridays, in the park in front of the school.
why: That is where Lin usually eats, but not on Fridays.
The note does not talk about a shop by the station.
Lin reads books at home in the evening. The note does not say Lin eats lunch there.
